item.title: Week 11 Game Recap: Bucs fall to 3-7; behind coaching woes
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Trevor Nowaske #53 of the Detroit Lions sacks Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the fourth quarter at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Knee deep in the midst of one of the most surreal playoff races that imaginable, the Buccaneers would be looking to collect a win against the Detroit Lions in week 11. Can Bucky Irving, Baker Mayfield, and the Bucs’ bodacious defense pull together to upset Dan Campbell’s bunch on the road? First Quarter: It was Baker Mayfield’s ball first on Sunday and it was his chance to get sacked first— One play, three defenders getting off their blocks, and one sack of Baker Mayfield with a forced fumble to boot. The Bucs stayed in possession only to punt and play defense. Jared Goff’s second pass and first completion of the day took Detroit across midfield, but two batted balls in a three play sequence forced the Lions into a long field attempt and long field goal miss. The Buccaneers’ offense found a few completions, a few third down conversions, and more importantly a bit of their stride. Tampa Bay moved nearly 50 yards to the Detroit 10-yard line before having to make a decision. Facing a fourth and one, Todd Bowles neglected a short field goal opportunity and chose to leave his offense on the field. Zac Robinson opted for Bucky Irving running into traffic and that traffic did more than slow him down, it stopped him. Tampa’s failed fourth down attempt jump started Detroit’s next drive. Second Quarter: 50% of Tampa’s star cornerback tandem would leave the field on Detroit’s second drive and for Todd Bowles’ defense, no Parrish = no good. The Lions tagged Benjamin Morrison for a big play and tagged him again for a touchdown. While Morrison did struggle to fill the Jacob Parrish’s shoes, one of the early death nails for Tampa’s defense though the early moments has been thorough inability to keep the Lions out of third down and one and a subsequent inability to stop Detroit from converting those third downs into first downs. 7-0, Lions. Tampa’s next start was kicked off by a false start— No doubt they had been holding that in, going an entire quarter without one. The Bucs’ next drive no longer featured third down as an unconquerable foe third downs— First down Cade Otton, first down Chris Godwin, however, old habits die hard— All out blitz, sack, punt. With the seems as open as a 7/11 in New York City, Jared Goff picked apart Tampa Bay’s zones all the way into the final two minutes of the half and field goal range. 10-0, Lions. Rocking a bad thumb, a bad foot, and a bad offense Baker Mayfield had a 1:30 from the 35-yard line to cut into the Lions’ lead. One more big scramble from the Buccaneers’ injured quarterback and rare down the field throw to Bucky Irving planted Tampa Bay squarely in Chase McLaughlin’s range. The Buccaneers did not choose to settle, they took a shot at the end zone, trying for six.

item.title: Ravens discussion: instant reactions to rollercoaster loss to Panthers
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens lost their sixth straight game on Sunday afternoon, falling to the Carolina Panthers by a score of 35-33. A back-and-forth matchup came down to the final drives, and once again, Baltimore’s defense could not get off the field during a late drive with the game on the line. Carolina took a two-point lead, setting Jacoby Brissett up for a potential game-winning score. Instead, he faced constant pressure in the pocket and had to throw up a prayer to avoid a sack that resulted in a game-ending interception. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the loss: Nikhil Mehta This game was drunk from the very start. The Ravens made their usual mistakes in all three phases – missed tackles, poor clock management, inept pass protection – but the Panthers tried to outdo them at every turn. There aren’t really any new takeaways. As in 2025, this team has been screaming at us, all year, that this is who they are. Jesse Minter’s Ravens simply cannot be at their best when the best is needed. In my opinion, their best is no longer needed. At 4-7, the season is effectively over. Winning out to snag a playoff spot – if that is even possible – is far-fetched even if Lamar Jackson comes back against the Steelers in Week 15. In fact, far-fetched might not be far enough. Baltimore is playing for a top-10 draft pick at this point. Maybe top-five. Kevin McNelis It almost feels worse to have the game be winnable at this point than to have the Ravens just get blown out. They had another double-digit lead, albeit early, which they squandered with miserable pass defense and multiple turnovers. Same stuff, different day. Now they have to worry about any lasting effects from a Derrick Henry concussion. At least Mike Green has started to show up big time. I like what I’m seeing from him, and if the Ravens can get Tavius Robinson to come back, they could have a pair of young EDGEs that would make it easier to build forward. Stephen Bopst It was simply another comedy of errors in Charlotte today. The Ravens continued their downward spiral by committing multiple errors that put a nail in their season. Justice Hill fumbled the ball out of the end zone, LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts, Derrick Henry fumbled, and to top it off Jacoby Brissett threw an awful game-ending pick. The Ravens were in position to win each of the last two games on the final drive but predictably gave the ball to the other team. Obviously, I want the Ravens to win, but continued losing is probably what it will take for some bigger changes to occur this off-season. Amongst all the other issues this year, I really am not seeing a lot of hope for the Jesse Minter led Ravens in the future. At the bare minimum, he was supposed to give this defense a boost which hasn’t come. Is it the players fault too? The Tampa Bay Buccaneers flew up and put up a fight, but it wasn’t enough, and they lost 31-21. The first half was low-scoring, but the offense exploded in the second half, and Tampa Bay couldn’t overcome it. Here are my five takeaways from the Lions’ victory against the Buccaneers. Front seven balled out We saw it against the Patriots last week, and again against the Bucs this week. Just because EDGE Aidan Hutchinson is out doesn’t mean this defensive line can’t still bring the juice. item.title: Here’s where the Falcons currently stand in the NFC South, the NFL’s weirdest division
item.description: Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images | Getty Images The Falcons are on their bye this week, but play continued in Week 11 for the rest of the NFC South — and it did shake up the standings a bit in a good way for the Falcons. The Panthers were the only NFC South team to win on Sunday, escaping with a narrow 2-point win over the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens and moving their record to 5-5. Carolina stays on top of the NFC South, and thanks to the other two teams losing, the Panthers extend their division lead to two games. The Buccaneers were facing the Lions in Detroit, and they lost 31-21. The Saints faced off against the Chicago Bears, and they lost 13-21. That evens up the Bucs, Saints, and Falcons at 3-7 through 11 weeks, and thanks to Atlanta’s head-to-head tiebreaker over New Orleans, the Saints drop down to the basement of this weird division. The Falcons are still eligible for the 2026 NFL playoffs, though I would not hold your breath. Fanduel Sportsbook has Atlanta’s odds to make the playoffs at +700, and while the Panthers’ two-game lead isn’t insurmountable with seven games left to play, I don’t think anyone who’s watched the Falcons play over the past few weeks is holding their breath for that outcome. item.title: Greenwich dethrones Staples on PKs in epic CIAC Class LL boys soccer championship
item.description: Members of the Greenwich boys soccer team celebrate after defeating Staples 3-2 (4-1 PKs) for the CAC Class LL championship on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026 at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford. (Will Aldam/Hearst Connecticut Media) HARTFORD - There was only one team expected to stay on its high horse as a CIAC boys soccer champion at Trinity Health Stadium this weekend. Only one team had a chance. That was Staples, a team even the opposing coach conceded was the best side in the state. But you know how things can go in the Wild West of sports. The plot can flip, the script riddled with holes, even high noon runs on to 3 p.m. Greenwich emerged as the new sheriff of Class LL boys soccer Sunday afternoon, knocking off top-seeded and defending champion Staples 3-2, on penalty kicks. The No. 6 Cardinals erased a 2-0 deficit in the second half and then dominated PKs 4-1, hitting all four of their shots while goalie Oliver Almeida turned two Staples attempts aside. It was the third state championship for Greenwich (15-4-3) and the team's first since 2022. Greenwich lost to Staples 3-0 in last year's final and the Wreckers (21-1-1) were undefeated going into their title defense. A 14th state title seemed fated when the Wreckers sprung to a 2-0 lead on a penalty kick by Adrian Rodriguez and a goal from Noah Rossoni. But Greenwich cut the deficit in half on a goal by MVP Shaun Liu with 26 minutes to play and Ebrima Touray delivered the equalizer with just over five minutes to go. After a scoreless overtime, Greenwich went 4-for-4 at the PK line behind Luca Ferrario, Sonny Warsing, Charlie Maniaci and Landon McFerran, while Almeida stopped two of the three attempts by Staples. Warsing and McFerran hadn't even been on the field during regulation and overtime, but when their number was called by coach Kurt Putnam, they were ready, and when McFerran drove home the fourth tally for Greenwich, it was over. Earlier, a Staples repeat seemed preordained. Just 5:25 in. Staples rushed the box, Almeida charged out and the ensuing contact resulted in a yellow card for Almeida and a penalty kick for Staples. item.title: Price wins Grand Slam to end wait for major title
item.description: Gerwyn Price has won the Grand Slam of Darts four times [Press Association] Gerwyn Price ended his four-year wait for a major PDC title as he powered to a brilliant 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final. The Welshman last won a major title when he claimed the World Series in 2022, but finally got over the line after defeats in three finals in 2026. The 41-year-old was the runner-up at the World Matchplay, World Grand Prix and World Series, as well as suffering semi-final exits in the Premier League, World Masters, UK Open and European Championships. This title has been long overdue and Price won it in spectacular fashion with a mid-match burst. Despite six breaks of throw in the opening 14 legs - including brilliant 150 and 145 checkouts from Price - the game was level at 7-7. But Price claimed a crucial lead in a scrappy 15th leg when he finally took out double two at the sixth attempt. That flicked a switch after a mini-interval and Price won the next five legs to open up a six-leg advantage. Van Veen broke back after another interval, but Price was able to hold off any hopes of a comeback from the Dutchman and seal his fourth Grand Slam title. "It's amazing - I've had some close calls this year when I probably should have won games and tournaments, but when it finally comes around it's nice," Price, who moves to world number three, told Sky Sports. item.title: ‘Turned Into the Weak Link on This Defense’ — Skip Bayless Points Out Caleb Downs’ Flaws As Cowboys’ Struggles Continue
item.description: ‘Turned Into the Weak Link on This Defense’ — Skip Bayless Points Out Caleb Downs’ Flaws As Cowboys’ Struggles Continue The Dallas Cowboys made bolstering their defense a priority in their offseason plans heading into the 2026 NFL season. Dallas drafted stellar safety Caleb Downs out of Ohio State in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Downs has been seeing action for the Cowboys and delivered at times. One longtime Dallas NFL observer, though, isn’t happy with what he’s been seeing out of Downs. Skip Bayless Rants Over Caleb Downs How has Downs played so far this season? In Sunday’s 51-30 rout of the Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium, the rookie safety finished with seven total tackles, including five solo stops, and added a tackle for loss. Coming into Week 11, Downs ranked 43rd on PFN’s Safety Impact Metric with a 74.7 grade. What in the world got under Skip Bayless’ skin about Downs? As Bayless watched the Titans-Cowboys game play out, he headed out to social media and shared these thoughts. Bayless wrote, “Caleb Downs has turned into the weak link on this defense. He’s mostly an undersized linebacker, run-player, blitzer. Struggles in coverage. 11th overall.” To be clear, though, the entire Cowboys defense has not been really good overall. Dallas defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who has been heavily criticized in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, saw his play-calling duties stripped. Mike Pettine took over that job just in time for Dallas’ big victory on Sunday. Both of those games, though, were losses for the Cowboys. Downs is just 21 years old and did come out of the college ranks with a level of fanfare. Bayless is primarily known for his takes from his days on ESPN’s “First Take” with Stephen A. Smith, but he also spent years covering the team for the now-defunct Dallas Times Herald newspaper. Rookies, no matter where they land in the NFL Draft, still need time to ramp up and learn the NFL style of playing defense. Downs will have his next opportunity to prove Bayless wrong when the Cowboys play their traditional Thanksgiving Day game. item.description: The Chicago Bears had a sloppy showing in their first week back from their bye, but they still managed to win their fifth straight game as they defeated the New Orleans Saints , 21-13, on Sunday. Simmons accounted for three of the Bears' five sacks against the Saints. He now has recorded at least one sack in his first three games with Chicago, totaling five sacks in that span. Chicago has recorded back-to-back "ugly" wins against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Saints, but there are no style points in the NFL. item.title: The Next Caleb Williams Conversation Could Get Very Expensive
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Bears have spent years trying to find a quarterback worth building around. The next conversation could involve finding out exactly how much keeping one will cost. Caleb Williams becomes eligible for a contract extension after this season. That does not mean a deal is imminent, or that Chicago has to rush into one. It does mean his next contract is moving from a distant consideration toward a decision the organization can actually make. And the numbers being discussed around the league are getting enormous. In a report examining the 2024 quarterback class, who will be eligible for extensions after the season, Front Office Sports’ Mark Maske spoke with agents and executives about which players could command top-of-the-market extensions. Williams received a particularly expensive endorsement. “I think that’s the guy you pay the most,” one NFL front-office executive told FOS. The executive was comparing Williams with his draft classmates. Six quarterbacks went in the first 12 picks in 2024, creating a group whose development has been followed almost as closely as its weekly results. Jun 9, 2026; Lake Forest, IL, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) talks with head coach Ben Johnson during Minicamp at Halas Hall. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Now comes another comparison: who gets paid, when it happens and how high the market has climbed by then. The same executive offered a qualification that makes the assessment more interesting than a simple declaration that Williams deserves a blank check. “None of those guys is a top-five quarterback in the league yet, to me,” the executive said. “ Caleb Williams is the closest to that. He’s close. But it’s more about whose turn it is. They’re the next guys in line, and you have to pay the going rate.” That is an outside evaluator’s opinion, not a Bears negotiating position. But it captures the awkward reality of quarterback contracts. A team is paying for the player it expects to have over the coming years. The price also reflects the available alternatives, the leverage involved and whatever another quarterback has just signed. Waiting for a player to satisfy every possible benchmark does not guarantee a more comfortable negotiation. Sometimes it simply gives the market time to move again. Maske reports that some league figures expect Lamar Jackson to become the first quarterback with a contract averaging $70 million annually this offseason. Whether Williams or another member of his class approaches or exceeds that figure remains an open question. There is no reported $70 million Bears offer. There is no reported Williams demand for that amount, either. For now, it is a potential market milestone that explains why the next round of quarterback extensions could look startling. item.title: If you’re worried about Arizona men’s basketball, don’t be
item.description: RJ Godfrey won’t save Arizona. Because Arizona need not be saved. Saying nothing of the ridiculousness that is Godfrey’s so-far failed attempts to get on the floor for the Wildcats, the team has proven to be pretty dang good without its presumed starting power forward. Concerns that followed the team’s opening night loss to UCLA have been gradually replaced with excitement as the team has won its last four, including a road win at Auburn and a home victory over No. 3 UConn. While nothing was or is ever guaranteed, it stood to reason that the Cats would be good again this season. Working against the team is an apparent lack of depth and, evidently, the shadow of last year’s team. Last year’s team, the won that finally ended the Final Four drought, was special. Not just in what it accomplished, but in what it was and had. A senior point guard. Stellar, polished freshmen. Three bigs — including one off the bench — who could have started for most teams in the nation and are or will be playing in the NBA someday. Last year’s team had advantages all over the floor, and it showed night in, night out. All of the analytics showed how generationally-good it was, likely only falling short of a national championship because another unicorn squad happened to exist. To expect anything similar would have been foolish and, simply, unfair. This year’s team was always going to a step or two below last year’s. Fun fact, though, most every team that Arizona ever puts on the court won’t measure up to the 2025-26 Cats. And that’s okay. From the looks of things early in the season it appears there is no truly dominant team, at least not on the level of last year’s Michigan or Arizona. There are plenty of good teams, a group with which the Cats reside. Are they flawed? Absolutely. But Arizona has Ivan Kharchenkov . It also had Mo Krivas and Caleb Holt . The three make up one of the best trios in the sport, and as long as they are healthy and on the floor you have to feel like a win is possible. If the team can get consistent contributions from Derek Dixon , JJ Mandaquit and any of the other bigs, you have to feel like a win is likely. And if Godfrey gets to take the floor in a game? You’d love to see it. Rebounds have been an issue at times, and the team hasn’t found as many easy buckets as you’d like. Godfrey, who at 6-foot-8 and 240 lbs is similar in size to Koa Peat , would figure to help there. While not a great player, he averaged 12.1 points and 5.4 rebounds per game last season for Clemson, making around 61 percent of his shots. Arizona sure could use him. And yet, the Cats are coming off a wire-to-wire win over a perennial Final Four contender in which the game was never truly in doubt at any time in the second half. What they had was enough, and while you’d like to see more than one point from the bench you can’t help but feel good having watched an Arizona that was essentially dared to shoot threes, and responded by making 10-of-22. item.description: Amorim’s Rabiot hope as Frenchman sends warning to Milan’s rivals: ‘We’re growing’ Adrien Rabiot believes Milan are growing as a team after he set up two goals against Frosinone. Ruben Amorim, meanwhile, has made it clear he wants the Frenchman’s contract renewal sorted soon. With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb , Rabiot spoke after the 5-1 win at San Siro , where he assisted Gonçalo Ramos and Ardon Jashari and controlled the game from start to finish. “Our problem is that we need to be focused for 90 minutes,” Rabiot said. “Today it went well, even if we conceded a bit at the end, but that’s normal. “We’re growing as a team: in the quality of our play, in our spirit and in our ability to make sacrifices for the whole game, all of us.” He also had a word for Ramos, who was taken off as a precaution: “He finally scored after a long time. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us and we have a lot of games, so I asked the coach to rest him a little. “Everyone’s attitude today was very positive, and we have to keep going like this.” ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Adrien Rabiot during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on November 22, 2026 in Italy. Gerry Cardinale was at the club’s headquarters this week to plan for the January window. According to Sky Sport, Rabiot’s renewal was among the topics discussed, with the club aiming to tie him down until 2031. There’s a reason for that. “With us, he’s the player who has to push the team forward. He’s the decisive element. With France, he has a different job to do, which shows how well he adapts to the team he’s in. “For me, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe. I hope his renewal comes soon.”

item.title: He was the two-time champion who also recorded the second-worst 72-hole score in Masters history
item.description: Photo by Augusta National/Getty Images Horton Smith’s Masters legacy is set in stone. Smith is recognised for having won 30 times in PGA Tour events, including eight victories during the 1929 season. However, it was during the 1930s that he secured the two most famous wins of his career. Smith won the first ever Masters in 1934, finishing one shot clear of Craig Wood. His second major title came at Augusta National two years later, with Harry Cooper the player to finish one shot adrift on that occasion. When Smith made his final appearance at The Masters in 1963, he was the last remaining player to have featured in every tournament. He had, however, failed to make it past the second round after Augusta National had introduced a 36-hole cut in 1957. Based on what happened one year earlier, he may not have been against the idea of the cut being brought in. How Horton Smith made more Masters history two decades after his two wins The 1956 Masters saw Jack Burke Jr. triumph with a winning score of one over par. It remains the highest winning score in Masters history, with Sam Snead and Zach Johnson also failing to break par when they were victorious at the iconic venue. Amateur Charles Kunkle made history by finishing the week at 52 over par. He failed to break 80 in the second and third rounds before posting a 95 on Sunday. Smith was only four shots better off after rounds of 86, 84, 84 and 82. It remains the second worst score that anyone has produced across four rounds at The Masters. With the cut coming in the following year, that statistic is highly unlikely to ever change. Smith faced a number of challenges in his later life. One year after he finished 48 over par in Georgia, he had a lung removed due to cancer. He went on to receive the Ben Hogan Award in 1960 having returned to the game. Sadly, however, Smith became the first Masters champion to pass away, with his death coming in 1963 at the age of 55. Smith retrospectively received his Green Jacket in 1949 when Augusta National decided to start awarding the garment to the champion each year. It was believed to have been lost for a number of years before eventually being put up for auction in 2013. It sold for $682,229.45, apparently making it the highest price paid for golfing memorabilia at the time. Smith meanwhile, would be posthumously inducted into the Golf Hall of Fame in 1990 – the same year Nick Faldo became the 13th player to win a second Masters title, 54 years after Smith had become the first.
